title: How to become an English teacher in Vietnam: step by step
description: The order that saves weeks: documents first, then certificate, job and work permit. Lead times, a week-by-week timeline, first-month cash and a checklist.
h1: How to become an English teacher in Vietnam: the steps, in the order that saves time and money
intro: To become an English teacher in Vietnam you need a bachelor's degree, a teaching certificate (most employers ask for 120 hours), a clean criminal record and a job offer from a school that files your work permit, which also asks for 2 years' relevant experience. Start the paperwork first: police checks and apostilles take weeks, and the check must be under 6 months old when your employer files. Ho Chi Minh City then publishes a 5-working-day decision; end to end, practitioners report one to six months.
keyPoints: **Documents first, job second.** Apostille (or legalise) your degree and order experience letters now; time the police check so it is no more than 6 months old on the day your employer files, which is 60 to 10 days before your start date.

The work-permit test under Decree 219/2025/ND-CP is a bachelor's degree plus at least 2 years' relevant experience. A TEFL, TESOL or CELTA does not replace the degree, and on its own it does not replace the experience; the law sets no minimum hours, and 120 hours is an employer convention.

Since 11 September 2026 an apostille replaces embassy legalisation for documents from the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa and the Philippines. German, Austrian and Czech documents, and Thai ones until 28 February 2027, still need full consular legalisation, and every document still needs a certified Vietnamese translation.

The employer files and pays the work-permit fee ({{vnd:600000}} in Ho Chi Minh City). You do the health check in Vietnam, and you may not teach until the permit is issued: the worker's fine is {{vnd:15000000-25000000}}, with possible deportation.

Bring at least {{vnd:21400000-24400000}} if you will rent a room, or {{vnd:48300000-60300000}} for a one-bedroom flat, to cover deposits and living costs until your first salary, which commonly arrives a month or more after you start. Hours build up slowly, so two to three months of living costs is a safer cushion if your pay is hourly.

sections.title: What you need before you start

blocks.text: Two sets of rules decide whether you can teach: the work-permit rules, which the labour side applies, and the education rules for the school or centre. Work permits rest on [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html), in force since 7 August 2025, which replaced the foreign-worker rules of Decrees 152/2020 and 70/2023. Guides that still quote '3 years' experience' are out of date. This is the short version.

items: **Degree and experience:** a bachelor's degree or higher plus at least 2 years' relevant experience for the work permit's 'expert' category (see below if you have less).
**Teaching certificate:** a 'suitable' TEFL, TESOL or CELTA; the law sets no minimum hours, and 120 hours is an employer convention.
**Criminal record:** issued no more than 6 months before the employer files, from your home country or Vietnam.
**Health check:** done in Vietnam in practice, because a foreign certificate counts only under a mutual-recognition agreement.

blocks.text: Non-native speakers, age limits and the gap between the law and what employers ask are covered in [requirements to teach English in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/requirements-to-teach-english-in-vietnam).
If you have less than 2 years' experience

Teachers are filed as 'experts', and an expert needs a bachelor's degree plus **at least 2 years of relevant work experience**. The usual proof is a letter from a past employer abroad stating your years of experience; experience gained in Vietnam counts only through earlier Vietnamese work permits. For experts working in education, Art 19(3) of the decree also lists, as an alternative proof, documents showing you meet the qualification standard set by education law. How Ho Chi Minh City applies that to a teacher with under 2 years' experience is not published.

So if that is you, ask the employer which proof they will file for you and get the answer in writing before you travel. Never use an experience letter that is not true: an employer that files altered or forged documents is fined {{vnd:40000000-60000000}} ({{vnd:80000000-120000000}} for a company, school or centre), and a permit issued in breach of the rules can be revoked.

sections.title: The steps in order, with lead times

blocks.text: The order matters because the slow parts are the documents from home, not the job search or the permit. A degree and experience letters never go stale, so do them first. The police check does go stale, so time it.

items.title: Ask past employers for experience letters
items.text: Lead time: depends entirely on your past employers, so ask first. Ask for letterhead, your job title, exact start and end dates, a signature and contact details. A reference letter is a private document, so it usually has to be notarised or certified by a solicitor before it can be apostilled.

items.title: Apostille or legalise your degree
items.text: Lead time: several weeks. Apostille offices are slow: the UK FCDO's paper service takes up to 25 working days plus post, and Global Affairs Canada's queue was about 25 business days in August 2026. Degree copies normally need a notary or solicitor first.

items.title: Get your teaching certificate
items.text: Lead time: about 4-5 weeks for a full-time CELTA or in-class 120-hour course; online courses run at your own pace. Get the certificate apostilled as well, since the education side checks it.

items.title: Order your national police check, then apostille it
items.text: Lead time: from days to several months by country, plus the apostille. Order it so that it will still be under 6 months old on the day your employer files. The clock runs from the issue date, not the apostille date.

items.title: Apply, interview and teach a demo lesson
items.text: Lead time: varies by employer and season. Get the offer in writing, including guaranteed hours, whether pay is gross or net, and who pays for each document step.

items.title: Travel when your employer is ready for you
items.text: In Vietnam you do the health check at a facility the employer names and have each apostilled document translated and certified, so the employer can file.

items.title: Your employer files the work permit
items.text: The employer files 60 to 10 days before your start date. The decree allows up to 10 working days for a decision; Ho Chi Minh City publishes 5.

items.title: Sign the labour contract, then start teaching
items.text: The written labour contract is signed after the permit is issued and before your start date. Do not teach a paid class before the permit exists. Your employer arranges the rest of your paperwork once your work permit is issued — ask them exactly what they cover and what it costs.

blocks.title: The mistake that costs the most time
blocks.text: A police check more than 6 months old on the filing date gets the dossier rejected, and courier and apostille delays often push home-country checks past that window. If your start date slips, check the issue date on your record before your employer files; reordering from abroad can take as long as the first time.

Vietnamese law asks only for a 'suitable' language-teaching certificate ([Circular 21/2018](https://luatvietnam.vn/giao-duc/thong-tu-21-2018-tt-bgddt-quy-che-to-chuc-hoat-dong-cua-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-166595-d1.html)); the 120-hour standard comes from employers, and big chains accept online courses of that length. A course with observed teaching practice with real learners makes you easier to hire, and top-tier employers prefer CELTA or Trinity CertTESOL. In Ho Chi Minh City, [Apollo IH runs CELTA](https://ihteachenglish.com/?p=13232) for {{vnd:42000000}}, or {{vnd:39500000}} if you pay at least 6 weeks before the start (fees as published in October 2026); check the centre's course page for the next dates. Whatever you choose, make sure the certificate states its hours and names an awarding body you can check. Our guide to [TEFL, TESOL and CELTA for Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/tefl-tesol-and-celta-for-vietnam) compares them in detail.

Foreign documents in a work-permit file must be legalised or apostilled, then translated into Vietnamese and certified. Vietnam joined the Apostille Convention with effect from **11 September 2026** ([HCCH status table](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41); [Decree 293/2026/ND-CP](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/7/293_2026_nd-cp_23072026_1-signed.signed.pdf)). Documents from member countries that did not object now need only an apostille from the country that issued them, and Vietnamese offices may not ask for legalisation on top. Documents from other countries still need consular legalisation. German, Austrian and Czech documents, and Thai ones until 28 February 2027, take the legalisation route. Documents legalised before 11 September 2026 stay valid.

Do things in this order: apostille first, translation second, so the translation also covers the apostille page. Since 1 July 2025 notaries no longer 'notarise translations'; a translation is made valid by certifying the translator's signature at a ward People's Committee or a notary office ([Nhân Dân](https://nhandan.vn/nhieu-quy-dinh-moi-ve-cong-chung-post892108.html)). Our guides to [getting your degree authenticated](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-your-degree-authenticated-for-vietnam) and the [criminal record check](/teach-in-vietnam/criminal-record-check-for-a-vietnam-work-permit) cover every country route in detail.

sections.title: Finding the job: from abroad or on the ground

blocks.text: Large employers interview overseas candidates by video: VUS, for example, runs an online application followed by a video interview with HR of about an hour ([VUS teacher site](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979)). Many smaller centres interview in person, and [International TEFL Academy](https://www.internationalteflacademy.com/teach-english-in-vietnam) says you usually need to be in Vietnam to interview. Some public-school agency ads ask for proof that you are already in the country. Demo lessons are common, sometimes taught to staff with no students present.

Searching on the ground gives you more interviews, but it does not let you skip the documents: your police check and degree still have to be apostilled in the country that issued them, which is slower to arrange from Vietnam. Either way, get the home-country papers moving before you fly, and do not teach until your permit is issued.

items: **Timing.** Language centres hire all year, busiest before and during the summer holiday (June to August) and slowest from mid-December until Tet. Public-school agency jobs follow the school year, September to May, so apply June to August. International schools recruit through their group portals and international job boards rather than local ads.

**Pay.** In July-October 2026 job ads, centres offered {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour, and most new-teacher offers fell between {{vnd:430000}} and {{vnd:560000}} ([Vietnam Teaching Jobs](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/city/teaching-english-in-ho-chi-minh)). 'Up to' rates are ceilings, so ask for guaranteed hours in writing.

**Location.** Since July 2025 Ho Chi Minh City includes former Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau, so a job labelled 'HCMC' can be far from District 1. Job ads still use the old district names, while official addresses now use new ward names.

**Where to look.** eno.vn's [teaching jobs](/jobs-vietnam-expats) link to the original posting where there is one, and you apply there; eno.vn has not verified the employers behind them. The [school directory](/schools) lists Ho Chi Minh City employers where teachers can vote and leave reviews, though most have few or none yet. A free profile at [teacher.eno.vn](https://teacher.eno.vn) lets schools and centres message you, and your contact details stay hidden until you choose to share them.

blocks.text: Never pay to get a job. Real employers do not charge application, placement or training fees, ask you to install an app or buy a flight through a recruiter's link; check that emails come from the employer's own domain. Our guides to [finding a teaching job](/teach-in-vietnam/finding-a-teaching-job-in-vietnam) and [spotting teaching job scams](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-job-scams-in-vietnam) go further.

sections.title: What your employer does for the work permit

blocks.text: The employer, not you, is the applicant. It files online through the National Public Service Portal or at a Public Administration Service Centre, and in Ho Chi Minh City the permit is issued by the **Department of Home Affairs** (Sở Nội vụ) for employers outside export-processing zones, industrial parks and high-tech parks, which covers practically every language centre and school ([Decision 6093/QĐ-UBND](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/quyet-dinh-6093-qd-ubnd-tp-ho-chi-minh-2026-cong-bo-danh-muc-thu-tuc-hanh-chinh-sua-doi-bo-sung-448197-d2.html), 21 September 2026). Your employer has the final word on what it needs from you and when.

blocks.text: The fee is set by [Resolution 09/2022/NQ-HĐND](https://luatvietnam.vn/thue/nghi-quyet-09-2022-nq-hdnd-239822-d2.html). A permit lasts up to 2 years and can be extended once by up to 2 years, then a new permit is needed. It is tied to one employer: changing employer needs a new permit. Since [Decision 526/QĐ-BNV](https://moha.gov.vn/Upload/a4c1b76d-88ab-49da-ac58-d23e8a518284Quyet%20dinh%20so%20526.QD-BNV.pdf) (13 May 2026), that permit no longer asks for your degree and experience proof if the job is the same and your current permit is still valid. A different job, or a permit that has already ended, means a full new application, so keep your apostilled originals and ask the new employer what it will file. Once your work permit is issued, your employer arranges the rest of your paperwork — ask them exactly what they cover and what it costs. Our [work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers) covers the whole procedure.

Working before the permit is issued is the costliest shortcut: under [Decree 283/2026/ND-CP](https://suckhoedoisong.vn/tu-10-9-2026-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-se-bi-phat-neu-khong-co-giay-phep-lao-dong-169260824224738.htm), in force since 10 September 2026, the worker is fined {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and may be deported. Before you sign, check the contract basics in the [Labour Code](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html): probation lasts at most 60 days at no less than 85% of the salary, and an employer may not keep your original documents or take a deposit. Our guide to [English teaching contracts](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam) lists what else to check.

sections.title: How much money to bring for the first month

blocks.text: Most centres pay monthly and by the teaching hour, and hours build up slowly, so the first salary commonly arrives a month or more after you start. The [eno.vn HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) puts the city-wide median asking rent at {{vnd:3900000}} a month for a room and {{vnd:6800000}} for a one-bedroom flat (snapshot 10 October 2026). Deposits are usually one to two months' rent plus the first month in advance.

blocks.caption: Cash needed in Ho Chi Minh City before your first salary (eno.vn estimate from October 2026 prices, assuming rents above the city-wide Rent Index medians of 10 October 2026; pre-departure document costs not included)

About {{vnd:200000}} for a SIM and plan
About {{vnd:300000}} for internet installation, if not included

blocks.text: Treat the total as a minimum: hours build up slowly and the first pay can come late, so keep a reserve on top; two to three months of living costs is a safer cushion if your pay is hourly. Big chains often cover a few nights' accommodation on arrival (ILA up to 6 nights and VUS 5 in their 2026 ads, Apollo up to 7 in its late-2025 ads), so ask what your employer provides. Before you pay a deposit, read our guide to [renting an apartment in Vietnam](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner). For monthly budgets once you are paid, see the [cost of living for a teacher in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/cost-of-living-in-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers).

Carry originals in your hand luggage and keep scans in the cloud. Hand employers certified copies, not originals; once in Vietnam, any ward People's Committee can [certify copies](https://lsvn.vn/tu-01-11-2025-ubnd-cap-xa-chung-thuc-cac-loai-giay-to-nao-a165222.html) of foreign-issued documents, wherever you live.

items: Your passport, plus a few colour photocopies of the photo page
Original degree with its apostille or legalisation, and your transcript
TEFL, TESOL or CELTA certificate with its apostille or legalisation
Police check, original and apostilled, with its issue date well inside the 6-month window
Experience letters on letterhead with your job title, exact dates, a signature and contact details, authenticated like your other documents
Any earlier Vietnamese work permits, which count as proof of experience
Proof of a name change, such as a marriage certificate or deed poll, apostilled, if your name differs across documents
Two or more 4x6 cm colour photos on a white background
Your CV, the employer's written offer and a printed demo lesson plan
Unlaminated originals: laminated certificates are refused by some apostille offices

faqs.q: Can I become an English teacher in Vietnam without a degree?
faqs.a: Not through the usual legal route. Teachers are filed as experts under Decree 219/2025/ND-CP, which requires a bachelor's degree or higher plus 2 years' relevant experience, and a TEFL certificate does not replace the degree. Teaching without a work permit risks a fine and deportation under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP.

faqs.q: Is there a maximum age to teach English in Vietnam?
faqs.a: The law sets a minimum age of 18 and no maximum for a work permit. Age limits in some job ads are employer or insurer preferences, so ask each employer directly.

faqs.q: Can non-native English speakers become teachers in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Yes. No law bars non-native speakers, and the work-permit test is the same degree and experience. At language centres, Circular 21/2018 asks non-native teachers for Level 5 (about C1) proof plus a teaching certificate; a degree in English replaces the Level 5 proof, and a degree in English teaching replaces both. Many employers still prefer native speakers, so expect a longer search.

faqs.q: Do I need my degree recognised by Vietnam's Ministry of Education?
faqs.a: Recognition by the Ministry of Education is not part of the work-permit dossier under Decree 219. The authority checks your apostilled or legalised degree together with a certified Vietnamese translation.

faqs.q: Can I use a Vietnamese criminal record instead of one from home?
faqs.a: Decree 219 accepts a criminal record from your home country or from Vietnam, and an employer can apply for the Vietnamese one online together with the work permit. Whether that works for someone who has only just arrived is not settled, so most people moving from abroad bring a home-country check. Ask your employer before you skip it.

faqs.q: Can I start teaching while my work permit is being processed?
faqs.a: No. Working before the permit is issued can mean a fine and deportation for you and a fine for the employer under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP. Ask your employer to confirm in writing that the permit has been issued before your first paid class.
